name: North Carolina
note: In North Carolina the funeral director who takes custody of the body notifies the local registrar within 24 hours and files the death certificate within five days, electronically through the state's NCDAVE system; the physician, PA or nurse practitioner certifies the cause within three days, and the county medical examiner takes violent, sudden, unattended and custodial deaths. The local registrar passes each certificate to the county register of deeds within seven days and the originals to the State Registrar monthly. Onward, the Department of Health and Human Services sends the State Board of Elections a weekly list of deceased residents for removal from the voter rolls, and the State Registrar sends the DMV a periodic list of deceased residents. Anyone may obtain a plain copy of a death record; certified copies are limited to family and people with a legal interest.

citations.title: Death; determination by physician
citations.quote: The determination that a person is dead shall be made by a physician licensed to practice medicine applying ordinary and accepted standards of medical practice.

citations.title: Medical examiner jurisdiction
citations.quote: shall be notified by a physician in attendance, hospital employee, law-enforcement officer, funeral home employee, emergency medical technician, relative or by any other person

citations.title: Death without medical attendance; notice to medical examiner
citations.quote: the funeral director or person acting as funeral director and any other person having knowledge of the death to notify the local medical examiner

citations.title: Death registration; five-day filing
citations.quote: shall be filed with the local registrar of the county in which the death occurred within five days after the death

citations.title: Funeral director files the death certificate
citations.quote: who first assumes custody of a dead body shall file the death certificate with the local registrar

citations.title: Medical certification of cause of death
citations.quote: completed and signed by the physician in charge of the patient's care for the illness or condition that resulted in death

citations.title: Medical certification within three days
citations.quote: shall complete the medical certification no more than three days after death

citations.title: Electronic filing via NCDAVE
citations.quote: Death certificates shall be filed electronically with the Office of Vital Records via the North Carolina Database Application for Vital Events (NCDAVE) system.

citations.title: Notification of death
citations.quote: shall submit a notification of death to the local registrar in the county where death occurred, within 24 hours of taking custody of the body

citations.title: Burial-transit permits
citations.quote: shall obtain a burial-transit permit signed by the medical examiner prior to final disposition or removal from the State and within five days after death.

citations.title: Medical examiner's permission before cremation
citations.quote: shall not be cremated or buried at sea unless a medical examiner certifies that he has inquired into the cause and the manner of death

citations.title: Misdemeanor
citations.quote: a person who violates a provision of this Chapter or the rules adopted by the Commission or a local board of health shall be guilty

citations.title: Duties of local registrars: transmission to register of deeds
citations.quote: transmit to the register of deeds of the county each certificate registered within seven days after receipt of a birth or death certificate

citations.title: Duties of local registrars: monthly transmission to the State Registrar
citations.quote: send to the State Registrar all original certificates registered during the preceding month

citations.title: Access to original vital records
citations.quote: Only the State Registrar shall have access to original vital records and to indices to the original vital records.

citations.title: Copies or abstracts to any person
citations.quote: provide copies or abstracts of vital records, except those described in subsections (d), (e), (f) and (g) of this section, to any person upon request

citations.title: Who may obtain certified copies
citations.quote: A person requesting a copy of the person's own vital records or that of the person's spouse, sibling, direct ancestor or descendant, or stepparent or stepchild

citations.title: Funeral directors entitled to certified death certificates
citations.quote: A funeral director or funeral service licensee shall be entitled upon request to a certified copy of a death certificate.

citations.title: List of deceased residents for the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles
citations.quote: The State Registrar shall provide to the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles an alphabetical list of all residents of the State who have died

citations.title: List maintenance: death (weekly DHHS list)
citations.quote: At a minimum of once per week, the Department of Health and Human Services shall furnish free of charge to the Executive Director

citations.title: List maintenance: death (statement by relative)
citations.quote: Upon receipt of a signed statement of a near relative or personal representative of the estate of a deceased voter indicating that the person has died

steps.title: Physician determines death
steps.who: A physician licensed to practise medicine.
steps.trigger: Cessation of life functions, including brain death.
steps.summary: The statute assigns the determination of death to a licensed physician applying ordinary and accepted standards of medical practice, and recognises brain death as a sole basis.

steps.title: Notify the county medical examiner
steps.who: A physician in attendance, hospital employee, law-enforcement officer, funeral home employee, EMT, relative or any other person with suspicion; for any death without medical attendance, the funeral director and anyone with knowledge.
steps.trigger: Death from violence, poisoning, accident, suicide or homicide; sudden death in apparent good health or unattended by a physician; death in jail, prison or police custody or a state facility; or suspicious, unusual or unnatural circumstances.
steps.summary: Deaths within medical examiner jurisdiction must be reported to the medical examiner of the county where the body is found, and the body may not be disturbed, removed or disposed of without the medical examiner's permission.

steps.title: Certify the medical cause of death in NCDAVE
steps.who: The physician in charge of the patient's care for the fatal illness; in their absence or with approval, an associate physician, PA, NP, the facility's chief medical officer, or an autopsy physician; failing all, any physician, PA or NP who makes reasonable inquiry.
steps.trigger: The death certificate is presented for medical certification.

deadline.text: no more than three days after death

steps.summary: The certifier states the cause in definite terms within three days (or marks it pending autopsy and supplements later). Certifiers may not refuse to certify through the electronic system; the Department may impose administrative penalties of $250 to $1,000 for wilful violations.

steps.title: Medical examiner certifies and permits disposition
steps.trigger: A death under medical examiner jurisdiction.

deadline.text: medical certification within three days; burial-transit permit within five days after death

steps.summary: In medical examiner cases the medical examiner completes the medical certification, and the funeral director must obtain a burial-transit permit signed by the medical examiner before disposition or removal from the state.

steps.title: Medical examiner certification before cremation
steps.trigger: Intended cremation or burial at sea.
steps.summary: A body may not be cremated or buried at sea unless a medical examiner certifies that they have inquired into the cause and manner of death and no further examination is needed. Deaths in a licensed hospital from natural disease alone, and deaths within 24 hours of birth, are exempt unless otherwise within ME jurisdiction.

steps.title: Funeral director's notification of death
steps.who: The funeral director or person acting as such who first assumes custody of the body.

deadline.text: within 24 hours of taking custody of the body

steps.summary: Within 24 hours of taking custody the funeral director notifies the local registrar of the county of death, naming the physician responsible for certification or, in ME cases, certifying the medical examiner's release of the body.

steps.title: File the death certificate
steps.who: The funeral director or person acting as funeral director who first assumes custody, with personal data from the next of kin or best qualified source.

deadline.text: within five days after the death

steps.summary: The funeral director obtains the medical certification, records the burial details, and files the certificate with the local registrar of the county of death within five days, electronically through NCDAVE. Violating the Public Health chapter is a misdemeanor unless otherwise provided.

steps.title: Local registrar sends the certificate to the register of deeds
steps.who: The local registrar, to the county register of deeds.
steps.summary: Using the method the State Registrar prescribes, the local registrar transmits each registered certificate to the county register of deeds, which issues certified copies locally.

steps.title: Originals to the State Registrar

deadline.text: on the fifth day of each month

steps.summary: On the fifth of each month (or more often on request) the local registrar sends the State Registrar all original certificates registered during the preceding month. Only the State Registrar has access to the original records.

steps.title: Certified copies to family and those with a legal interest
steps.who: The State Registrar and other officials authorised to issue certified copies (registers of deeds).
steps.summary: Certified copies go only to the person, their spouse, sibling, direct ancestor or descendant, stepparent or stepchild, a person seeking a legal determination of personal or property rights, or their authorised agent, attorney or legal representative. Funeral directors are entitled to certified copies of death certificates.

steps.title: Weekly list of deceased residents to the State Board of Elections
steps.who: The Department of Health and Human Services, to the Executive Director of the State Board, who distributes names to county boards of elections.

deadline.text: at a minimum of once per week

steps.summary: DHHS furnishes the names of deceased residents free of charge at least weekly; each county board removes them from its voter registration records each week.

steps.title: Relative's statement removes a deceased voter
steps.who: A near relative or the personal representative of the estate.

deadline.text: county board removes the voter within one week of receipt

steps.summary: On a signed statement from a near relative or personal representative, the county board removes the voter within a week, without sending notice to the voter's address.

steps.title: List of deceased residents to the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles
steps.trigger: Periodic cycle tied to the jury list.

deadline.text: residents who died in the two years before 1 July of each odd-numbered year (yearly when an annual jury list is prepared)

steps.summary: The State Registrar gives the DMV Commissioner an alphabetical list, printed or computerised, of residents who died, with name and address. The statute ties the list to jury-list preparation; what DMV does with it is not stated here.

steps.title: Uncertified copies or abstracts to any person
steps.who: The State Registrar and other officials authorised to issue copies.
steps.summary: Apart from protected birth data and adoption, health and witness-protection records, copies or abstracts of vital records must be provided to any person on request, so a bank or insurer can obtain a plain copy of a death record. Certified copies remain restricted; no statutory data service or duty on private bodies was found.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Death certificate filed with the local registrar within five days; notification of death within 24 hours of custody; medical certification within three days.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director or person acting as such who first assumes custody files the certificate, with personal data from the next of kin.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No review of every certificate, but a medical examiner must certify before any cremation or burial at sea, except natural hospital deaths and deaths within 24 hours of birth.

electronicRegistration.note: Death certificates must be filed electronically via NCDAVE, and certifiers may not refuse to certify through it.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the State Registrar holds the original vital records.

governmentPropagation.note: Weekly DHHS feed to the State Board of Elections and a periodic list to the DMV; Social Security notification is in the federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: Copies or abstracts to any person; certified copies to close family, persons with a legal interest, their representatives and funeral directors.

privateSectorVerification.note: Private bodies may obtain an uncertified copy of a death record like anyone else; no official verification service or duty to check was found.

gaps: No North Carolina statute was found authorising registered nurses to pronounce death; G.S. 90-323 speaks only of physicians. Nurse pronouncement may rest on Board of Nursing rules, which were not checked.
No state statute was found requiring an EDR feed to SSA, notification of NC Medicaid (DHB) or the Department of Revenue; any such feeds are administrative and not sourced here.
G.S. 130A-121 does not say what the DMV does with the list of deceased residents (licence cancellation was not found in Chapter 20).
Rules of the Commission for Public Health on vital records (10A NCAC 41H) were not read.
Probate notice to creditors (G.S. 28A-14-1) was not researched as a public-notice step.
